messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: Routing tier spillover alert — high 5xx rate from eu-west-1, automated failover triggered to us-east-1 (severity: P1). See alert: https://alerting.redwood.internal/INC-19225 :rotating_light:

sre-oncall-mia: taking this. I’m oncall — gathering initial blast radius. :eyes:

josh: I see elevated tail latency at the load balancer around 10:14 UTC, + errors spiking at 10:16. Dumping initial stats now.

ana: (from monitoring) request volume to eu-west-1 jumped 3x between 10:10-10:15 due to retries from a downstream client, then routing policy sent overflow to us-east-1.

kev: any obvious config changes? deploy-bot show-deploys --since 2h

deploy-bot: deploys in last 2h: none in eu-west-1, 1 canary in us-east-1 (10:05) by eng-runtime-ryan — no rollbacks.

eng-runtime-ryan: that canary was model-vert:v2026-03 (quantized). It passed smoke. Not related?

cust-success-lina: we have 2 customers reporting degraded responses for their EU users. CC: pm-nina.

pm-nina: noted. What’s the mitigation plan? Do we fail open to older model?

sre-oncall-mia: live mitigation: 1) pause overflow routing to us-east (stop spillover) 2) enable fallback to local smaller model in eu-west (v1-proto) 3) throttle retrying clients via rate-limit header. Applying step 1 now.

josh: mia — can you paste the routing command?

sre-oncall-mia: sudo rctl routing modify --policy tier-spillover --region eu-west-1 --overflow=false

ana: confirmed overflow disabled. New routing decisions should keep to eu-west primary (but be aware capacity limited).

kev: while overflow was enabled, some requests hit a model variant that didn’t have compatible kv-cache layout and returned model-mismatch errors. Scraping logs.

josh: log snippet from proxy (10:16:12):

```
[10:16:12] proxy-req id=abc123 route=us-east-1 backend=model-vert:v2026-03 error=KV_CACHE_MISMATCH seq=256
[10:16:12] proxy-req id=abc124 route=us-east-1 backend=model-vert:v2026-03 error=COMPAT_LAYER_TIMEOUT seq=257
```

eng-runtime-ryan: those errors look like the quantized variant had a different KV cache tag after an optimization landed in the runtime last week. Hmm.

ana: timeline so far: 10:05 canary in us-east, 10:10 retry storm starts, 10:14 lb latency rises, 10:16 overflow engages, 10:16-10:18 KV cache errors spike, 10:20 customers start reporting.

pm-nina: assigning impact assessment: Lina — please collect customer IDs and affected regions and severity.

cust-success-lina: Will do. Two accounts: AcmeCorp (eu users), BetaApps (eu+apac). Both report 5-10s latency and occasional 5xx payloads.

kev: hypothesis A: spillover routing sent traffic to a model variant (v2026-03-quant) with incompatible KV layout due to runtime change -> errors and retries -> cascade.

kev: hypothesis B: the spillover threshold in the routing policy uses an absolute token backlog metric that undercounts CPU-limited queues; overflow decision was too eager -> overloaded us-east pool -> rate limiter thrash.

ana: evidence for A: consistent KV_CACHE_MISMATCH in us-east logs correlated with routing timestamps. Evidence for B: us-east GPU utilization reached >95% immediately after overflow turned on.

josh: can we confirm which backends served the 5xx p75? query: SELECT backend, count(*) FROM proxy_logs WHERE ts BETWEEN 10:15 AND 10:20 GROUP BY backend ORDER BY count DESC

eng-runtime-ryan: quick dump: model-vert:v2026-03 (us-east) -> 1,240 errors; model-stable:v1-proto (eu-west) -> 120 errors.

sre-oncall-mia: mitigation step 2: enabling fallback_to_local_model in eu-west now to reduce impact while we fix routing. Command: sudo rctl routing modify --region eu-west-1 --fallback v1-proto --enable=true

deploy-bot: fallback to v1-proto deployed in eu-west. Observability: latency down ~30% within 2 minutes.

ana: customers still seeing occasional errors but overall recovery trend. Keep overflow disabled until further investigation.

kev: next actions for RCA: - capture kernel logs and runtime trace from a failing worker in us-east - snapshot routing policy config at time of spillover - collect sequence of model rollouts and kernel patch merges in last 7 days - validate KV cache tag compatibility matrix

josh: grabbing us-east worker trace now. Pasted trace ID: trace-usr-19225-01. Relevant tail:

```
trace-usr-19225-01: runtime_init -> kernel_select(quant_kern_v3) -> load_kv_cache(tag=0x7a1c) -> expect_tag=0x4b2f -> mismatch -> abort_seq
```

eng-runtime-ryan: that confirms tag mismatch on quant_kern_v3 introduced by kernel selection change. I’ll bisect the runtime patch that modified tag generation.

pm-nina: who owns routing policy math? ana?

ana: yes, routing policies are on eng-platform but coordinated with eng-runtime for compatibility. I’ll open tracking issue.

sre-oncall-mia: ownership and actions for the rest of the incident:
- ryan: runtime bisect + revert candidate for tag mismatch (ETA 60m)
- ana: snapshot+postmortem of spillover threshold logic + add unit test (ETA 90m)
- kev: collect full log set and prepare RCA draft (ETA 120m)
- josh/mia: continue monitoring and maintain customer comms (live)

cust-success-lina: I’ll update affected customers with a summary and planned fix ETA.

josh: added quick mitigation checklist to the incident doc: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/19225-mitigation (links to runbooks: routing-fallback, kv-cache-compat).

eng-runtime-ryan: preliminary find: runtime kernel tag change introduced in CL 4567 (merged 3 days ago). Reverting that CL on a canary in us-east to validate.

deploy-bot: canary revert initiated for runtime-canary-us-east at 10:48 UTC by eng-runtime-ryan.

sre-oncall-mia: customers: Lina, please add concise note to AcmeCorp & BetaApps that we are actively rolling a revert and expect full restore within 1-2 hours.

cust-success-lina: note sent. Tone: apology + technical summary + ETA.

ana: root-cause hypothesis (working): automated spillover policy engaged during a transient retry storm, routing directed traffic to a quantized model variant that had an incompatible KV cache tag because of a recent runtime kernel change -> rapid error amplification and overloaded fallback pool -> customer impact.

kev: counters: how did overflow get enabled with such low gating? We need a post-incident config audit. Adding to tasks.

eng-runtime-ryan: canary revert shows reduced KV_CACHE_MISMATCH events in us-east canary after 6 minutes. If this continues we’ll promote revert.

sre-oncall-mia: promoting revert to stable in us-east will be our remediation if canary holds. Waiting on 10 more minutes of successful telemetry.

josh: recording timeline and flags in thread. Will stitch into final RCA.

pm-nina: thanks everyone. Please add any missing logs/links to the incident doc. We’ll have a formal RCA doc after wrap. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to P2 at 10:58 UTC after rollback canary proved successful. Full stable rollout scheduled pending post-checks.

sre-oncall-mia: marking handoff to oncall+RCA owners — I'll stay attached for postmortem notes. Closing live mitigation channel in 30m unless new regressions.

kev: final note for RCA: recommend immediate guardrails — disallow overflow to region unless backend compatibility matrix verified and add a pre-spill compatibility check.

eng-runtime-ryan: will prepare revert PR details and a compatibility test plan.

ana: opening tracking issue: https://issues.redwood.internal/INC-19225-rootcause — will add tasks and assignees.

cust-success-lina: customers acknowledged ETA and will follow up if anything else.

josh: adding post-incident action items to sprint. Night crew — keep an eye on routing alerts.

sre-oncall-mia: thanks all, great cross-team response. We’ll reconvene for RCA write up at 14:00 UTC.
